newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus to produce 1.81 mln t crude in '97 - adviser.
newsitem.headline: Belarus to produce 1.81 mln t crude in '97 - adviser.

text.p: Belarus expects crude oil production to fall to 1.81 million tonnes (about 36,200 barrels per day) in 1997 from 1.86 million tonnes (37,200 bpd) in 1996, a presidential adviser said on Tuesday.

"Oil production will fall every year because there is inadequate funding for it from the state budget," said Nikolay Polyavko, who advises President Alexander Lukashenko on the state oil concern Belnefteprodukt.
He also said 50 percent of reserves in the Prypyat well, the only well in the former Soviet republic, were depleted.
"Oil production will no longer increase since it's getting more difficult and we have to drill deeper," Polyavko said.
Belnefteprodukt has forecast a decrease in production of one percent annually.
The former Soviet republic requires 10-12 million tonnes (200,000-240,000 bpd) of oil yearly to meet domestic needs, and most of it is imported from Russia.
